title: Ultrahigh tribocorrosion resistance of metals enabled by nano-layering

nodes.label: Metals in corrosive service lose material fastest when sliding wear and corrosion act together (tribocorrosion)

attrs.note: no introduction in packet; need framed from title and domain knowledge

nodes.label: Nano-layering Al with a second metal at ~3 nm should give ultrahigh tribocorrosion resistance

requires_unseen: title: 'Ultrahigh tribocorrosion resistance of metals enabled by nano-layering'

nodes.label: Equal-spaced Al/X multilayer: ~3 nm per layer, ~6 nm bilayer, ~1.74 um total on Si

attrs.image_note: schematic annotations '~3nm', '~6nm', '~1.74um', 'Si'

nodes.label: Second metal X = Ti, Mg or Cu; monolithic Al, Ti, Mg and Cu films as controls

attrs.image_note: F1a annotation 'Mg, Ti, and Cu'; F4a legend Pure Ti/Mg/Cu/Al

nodes.label: DC magnetron sputtering of alternating X and Al layers onto (100) Si, X first

requires_unseen: DC magnetron sputtering, 5 mTorr Ar, (100) Si, X deposited first (linked text F1)

nodes.label: Films are periodic nanolayers with a bilayer period of ~5-6 nm

requires_unseen: Cu Kalpha wavelength 1.5406 A needed to convert the XRR peak position to a bilayer period (linked text F1)
TEM bilayer thicknesses (Table 1) agree with XRR (linked text F2)
attrs.image_note: Al/Mg periodicity weakly resolved: faint XRR peak, no TEM layer contrast

nodes.label: Hardness ranks Al/Cu (~6.3 GPa) > Al/Ti (~5.4 GPa) > Al/Mg (~3.8 GPa)
Quasi-steady nanowear rate is lowest for Al/Cu and highest for Al/Mg
Galvanic coupling between layers: Al corrodes sacrificially in Al/Ti and Al/Cu, Mg is the anode in Al/Mg

requires_unseen: F8 panels are FE-simulated corrosion in 0.6 M NaCl with dashed lines = original surface (caption and linked text F8)
galvanic sacrificial-anode reading (linked text F8)
attrs.image_note: FE simulation renders; layer identities from in-image labels

nodes.label: Corrosion resistance ranks Al/Ti (lowest current, stable passive branch) > Al/Cu > Al/Mg
Ti beneath the Al surface raises the work function, making electron loss harder and lowering surface activity

requires_unseen: higher work function = electron loss harder = reduced surface activity (linked text F10)

nodes.label: Ti beneath the Al surface weakens Cl adsorption, lowering the tendency to take up aggressive chloride

requires_unseen: less negative Cl adsorption energy = lower tendency to adsorb Cl and pit (linked text F10)
attrs.note: split from n12 by judge; O adsorption difference (3.1%) is small and not argued

nodes.label: Tribocorrosion material loss is smallest for Al/Cu, slightly larger for Al/Ti and far largest for Al/Mg

requires_unseen: the test is tribocorrosion (sliding in 0.6 M NaCl), stated in caption F6 and linked text

nodes.label: Sliding strips the passive film from the track (depassivation), shifting OCP cathodically until repassivation

requires_unseen: OCP was recorded while sliding in 0.6 M NaCl (caption F6)
depassivation/repassivation reading of the OCP drop (linked text F6)
attrs.image_note: depassivation shown clearly only for Al/Ti (86 mV drop); Al/Mg and Al/Cu drops are 8 and 1.6 mV

nodes.label: The worn track becomes an anode galvanically coupled to the unworn cathode, so corrosion accelerates in the track

requires_unseen: F9d-f show FE current density during tribocorrosion (caption F9)
arrows are current lines with thickness proportional to current density; worn-anode/unworn-cathode coupling (linked text F9)
blue F6d bars are FE-predicted corrosion current (caption F6)
attrs.image_note: FE current ranking matches wear-volume order but not its ratios (see o25)

nodes.label: Tribocorrosion damage mode: plastic deformation in Al/Ti, corrosion-dominated attack in Al/Mg and Al/Cu
Nano-layered Al/X films resist tribocorrosion by combining size-strengthened wear resistance with Al-led passivity; Al/Cu best, Al/Mg worst here

requires_unseen: title claim 'ultrahigh tribocorrosion resistance'
linked text F6: Al/Cu best because of highest wear resistance

nodes.label: Al/Ti and Al/Cu stack textured close-packed planes (Al{111}||Ti{0002}, Cu{111}) across semi-coherent interfaces

requires_unseen: semi-coherent interface classification (linked text F2)

nodes.label: NMM hardness is 3-5 times the rule-of-mixture hardness of the constituent films

requires_unseen: Tables 1-2 hardness and rule-of-mixture values (not in packet)

nodes.label: When wear events are infrequent and corrosion dominates loss, Al/Ti should be the most tribocorrosion-resistant NMM

requires_unseen: linked text F6: expectation for a lower wear frequency

nodes.label: Passive film on Al/Ti stays n-type over the scanned range; on Al/Mg it turns p-type at anodic potentials

requires_unseen: Mott-Schottky slope-sign rule: positive = n-type, negative = p-type (linked text F4, k4)
the measured capacitance is that of the passive film (linked text F4)
attrs.note: Al/Cu excluded from the label: its negative-slope segment (-0.32 to -0.27 V) lies below the marked E_OCP

nodes.label: Archard's law: wear volume scales inversely with hardness
When grain size d >> layer thickness h, h is the controlling length scale for NMM strength

requires_unseen: linked text F2, ref [44]; grain sizes 75-179 nm vs h = 3 nm

nodes.label: Mott-Schottky relation: 1/C^2 linear in E; positive slope = n-type donors, negative = p-type, slope gives defect density

requires_unseen: equation and slope-sign rule in linked text F4 (eps = 10 for Al2O3)

notes: Spine: tribocorrosion need -> nano-layering hypothesis -> 3 nm Al/X architecture + X sweep (Ti, Mg, Cu) -> sputtering -> periodic nanolayers -> branch A hardness -> wear rate; branch B galvanic MEC + DFT surface MEC -> corrosion ranking -> tribocorrosion loss (joint causes) explained by wear-accelerated corrosion MEC and damage-mode class -> conclusion. Audits: o10 running-in wear reversal, o16 EDS 'C' map (no Cu map) under the Cu-enrichment claim, o21 Al/Ti highest donor density. Packet: F2 and F7 are tagged C3_caption_swap but both images match their captions; F10d not offered (crop F10c holds c+d, F10e holds e+f); F6b crop has OCR cue 'micrograph' on a COF plot (not cited). Linked text F9 cites 'Fig. 8(d)' for the wear-volume trend, which is F6d. Not in graph: COF (F6b: Al/Ti ~0.38, Al/Cu ~0.27, Al/Mg ~0.16), repassivation times, F9a-c stress maps, grain sizes (text), XPS (supplement).
